topics.title: My Daily Routine
topics.description: Talk about the things you do every day.
topics.objective: Practise describing daily habits using simple present tense.
topics.opening_message: Hi there! I'd love to hear about a normal day for you — what time do you usually wake up?
topics.instructions: Encourage simple present tense and time expressions like 'usually', 'always', 'every day'. Keep questions short and concrete. Praise correct verb forms gently.
topics.vocabulary_focus: daily routine, wake up, get dressed, have breakfast, go to bed
topics.grammar_focus: simple present tense for habits

topics.title: My Family
topics.description: Describe the members of your family.
topics.objective: Practise family vocabulary and simple descriptions.
topics.opening_message: Good morning! Can you tell me a little about your family — how many people are in it?
topics.instructions: Focus on family vocabulary and simple adjectives for describing people. Ask about names, ages, and jobs. Keep sentences short.
topics.grammar_focus: possessive adjectives (my, his, her)

topics.title: My Home
topics.description: Describe your house or apartment.
topics.objective: Practise describing rooms and furniture with simple present tense.
topics.opening_message: Hello! I'm curious about where you live — can you describe your home to me?
topics.instructions: Guide the learner through rooms, furniture, and basic prepositions of place. Use simple 'there is/there are' structures. Correct basic vocabulary gently.
topics.vocabulary_focus: living room, kitchen, bedroom, furniture, apartment
topics.grammar_focus: there is / there are, prepositions of place

topics.title: Food I Like
topics.description: Talk about your favourite foods and meals.
topics.objective: Practise talking about likes and dislikes with food vocabulary.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Food is always fun to talk about — what's your favourite meal to eat?
topics.instructions: Encourage 'I like / I don't like' structures and simple food vocabulary. Ask about breakfast, lunch, dinner preferences. Keep it light and friendly.
topics.grammar_focus: like/love/hate + noun or gerund

topics.title: My Hobbies
topics.description: Share what you enjoy doing in your free time.
topics.objective: Practise describing hobbies and free-time activities.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Everyone has something they love doing after work or school — what's your favourite hobby?
topics.instructions: Ask simple follow-up questions about frequency and reasons. Encourage present simple and basic connectors like 'because'. Keep vocabulary everyday.
topics.vocabulary_focus: hobby, free time, enjoy, relax, play
topics.grammar_focus: simple present with adverbs of frequency

topics.title: Talking About Weather
topics.description: Describe today's weather and your favourite season.
topics.objective: Practise weather vocabulary and simple descriptions.
topics.opening_message: Good day! I'm wondering — what's the weather like where you are right now?
topics.instructions: Focus on basic weather adjectives and seasons vocabulary. Ask about clothing choices related to weather. Keep exchanges short and clear.
topics.grammar_focus: simple present for facts, adjectives

topics.title: My Pet or a Pet I'd Like
topics.description: Talk about a pet you have or would like to have.
topics.objective: Practise simple descriptions and preferences about animals.
topics.opening_message: Hi again! Do you have a pet, or is there an animal you'd love to have one day?
topics.instructions: Ask about the pet's name, appearance, and daily care if they have one. If not, explore what animal they'd choose and why. Keep language simple.
topics.grammar_focus: simple present, would like to

topics.title: Going Shopping
topics.description: Talk about a recent shopping trip.
topics.objective: Practise past simple for a short shopping story.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Let's chat about shopping — when was the last time you went shopping, and what did you buy?
topics.instructions: Encourage basic past simple verbs (bought, went, paid). Ask where they shopped and how they felt about it. Keep vocabulary concrete and simple.
topics.grammar_focus: past simple regular and irregular verbs

topics.title: School or Work
topics.description: Describe your school or workplace.
topics.objective: Practise simple present tense to describe daily study or work life.
topics.opening_message: Hi there! Tell me a bit about your school or your job — what do you do there?
topics.instructions: Ask about a typical day, people they see, and simple opinions (easy/hard/fun). Keep grammar at simple present level. Encourage full sentences.
topics.grammar_focus: simple present for routines

topics.title: Getting Around Town
topics.description: Talk about how you usually travel around your city.
topics.objective: Practise vocabulary for transportation and simple present tense.
topics.opening_message: Hey! I'm curious how you get around — do you usually walk, drive, or take the bus?
topics.instructions: Focus on transportation vocabulary and simple reasons (fast, cheap, convenient). Ask about a typical commute. Keep questions concrete.
topics.grammar_focus: simple present, prepositions of transport (by, on)

topics.title: My Friends
topics.description: Describe your closest friends and how you met them.
topics.objective: Practise describing people and simple past for meeting stories.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Friends make life more fun, don't they? Can you tell me about a good friend of yours?
topics.instructions: Ask how they met, what they do together, and simple personality adjectives. Encourage past simple for the meeting story. Keep it warm and personal.
topics.vocabulary_focus: friendly, kind, funny, meet, hang out
topics.grammar_focus: past simple for meeting someone

topics.title: Morning Person or Night Person
topics.description: Talk about whether you prefer mornings or evenings.
topics.objective: Practise simple opinions and reasons using basic connectors.
topics.opening_message: Good to see you! Quick question to start — are you more of a morning person or a night person?
topics.instructions: Ask for simple reasons using 'because'. Keep the exchange light and encourage short explanations. Correct basic word order gently.
follow_up_directions: best time of day to study
topics.vocabulary_focus: morning person, night owl, tired, energetic
topics.grammar_focus: simple present, because + reason

topics.title: A Recent Trip
topics.description: Talk about a trip or short vacation you took recently.
topics.objective: Practise past simple to narrate a short travel experience.
topics.opening_message: Hi! I love hearing travel stories — have you taken any trips lately that you could tell me about?
topics.instructions: Encourage past simple narration with time markers (last month, two weeks ago). Ask about the place, activities, and feelings. Help expand short answers into fuller sentences.
topics.grammar_focus: past simple narrative with time expressions

topics.title: Social Media Habits
topics.description: Discuss how you use social media in daily life.
topics.objective: Practise present simple and opinions about technology habits.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Social media is everywhere these days — which apps do you use most, and why?
topics.instructions: Ask about frequency, favourite platforms, and pros/cons. Encourage simple opinion phrases like 'I think' and 'in my opinion'. Keep the tone conversational.
topics.grammar_focus: present simple, expressing opinions

topics.title: Favourite Time of Year
topics.description: Talk about your favourite season and why you like it.
topics.objective: Practise giving reasons and describing seasonal activities.
topics.opening_message: Hello! If you could pick, which season would you say is your favourite one?
topics.instructions: Ask learners to justify their choice with specific activities or memories. Encourage comparative language (better than, warmer than). Keep vocabulary seasonal.
topics.grammar_focus: comparatives, giving reasons

topics.title: A Memorable Meal
topics.description: Describe a meal you'll never forget.
topics.objective: Practise past simple storytelling with descriptive food vocabulary.
topics.opening_message: Hi there! Think back — is there a meal that really stands out in your memory? Tell me about it.
topics.instructions: Guide the learner to describe where, when, who, and why it was memorable. Encourage descriptive adjectives for taste and atmosphere. Help with past tense accuracy.
topics.grammar_focus: past simple, descriptive adjectives

topics.title: Learning a New Language
topics.description: Talk about your experience learning English or another language.
topics.objective: Practise talking about ongoing learning experiences and challenges.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Learning a new language is a journey — what's been the hardest part for you so far?
topics.instructions: Ask about study methods, challenges, and small wins. Encourage present perfect for experience (I have learned, I have tried). Be supportive and encouraging.
topics.grammar_focus: present perfect for experience

topics.title: Staying Healthy
topics.description: Discuss habits you have for staying fit and healthy.
topics.objective: Practise talking about health habits using simple present and frequency adverbs.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Let's talk health — what do you usually do to stay fit and feel good?
topics.instructions: Ask about exercise, sleep, and eating habits. Encourage frequency adverbs (often, rarely, never). Keep advice-giving light and non-judgmental.
topics.grammar_focus: adverbs of frequency with present simple

topics.title: Money and Saving
topics.description: Talk about how you manage your money.
topics.objective: Practise talking about habits and simple financial vocabulary.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Managing money can be tricky — do you consider yourself a saver or a spender?
topics.instructions: Ask about saving habits, budgeting, and one recent purchase. Keep grammar at simple present/past level. Avoid giving financial advice; focus on language.
topics.grammar_focus: simple present and past for habits and events

topics.title: A Typical Weekend
topics.description: Describe what you usually do on weekends.
topics.objective: Practise present simple and sequencing words for routines.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Weekends are always interesting — what does a typical Saturday look like for you?
topics.instructions: Encourage sequencing words (first, then, after that). Ask about differences between weekdays and weekends. Keep tone relaxed and friendly.
topics.vocabulary_focus: relax, chores, errands, sleep in, weekend
topics.grammar_focus: sequencing words with present simple

topics.title: Technology in Everyday Life
topics.description: Talk about the gadgets and technology you use daily.
topics.objective: Practise describing technology use and simple opinions.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Technology is a big part of life now — what gadget could you absolutely not live without?
topics.instructions: Ask about specific devices, apps, and how technology has changed their daily routine. Encourage comparison with the past (used to). Keep it conversational.
topics.grammar_focus: used to for past habits vs now

topics.title: Public Transportation Experiences
topics.description: Share an experience using buses, trains, or subways.
topics.objective: Practise narrating a specific past experience with transportation.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Have you had any interesting experiences on public transportation? Tell me about one.
topics.instructions: Ask for a specific story with past simple. Encourage details about people, delays, or funny moments. Help connect ideas with 'and then', 'but'.
topics.grammar_focus: past simple narrative, sequencing

topics.title: Celebrations and Holidays
topics.description: Talk about a holiday or celebration you enjoy.
topics.objective: Practise describing traditions and cultural events.
topics.opening_message: Hi there! Every culture has special celebrations — what's a holiday you really enjoy?
topics.instructions: Ask about traditions, food, and family involvement. Encourage present simple for traditions and past simple for specific memories. Be curious about cultural details.
topics.grammar_focus: present simple for traditions, past simple for memories

topics.title: City Life vs Countryside Life
topics.description: Compare living in a city with living in the countryside.
topics.objective: Practise comparative structures while discussing lifestyle differences.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Some people love busy cities, others prefer quiet countryside — which do you prefer?
topics.instructions: Encourage comparative and superlative forms (busier, quieter, the best). Ask for concrete reasons and personal experience. Keep the discussion balanced.
topics.grammar_focus: comparatives and superlatives

topics.title: Music You Love
topics.description: Talk about the music and artists you enjoy.
topics.objective: Practise expressing preferences and simple opinions about music.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Music says a lot about us — what kind of music do you usually listen to?
topics.instructions: Ask about favourite artists, genres, and when they listen to music. Encourage simple opinion language and reasons. Keep the tone upbeat.
topics.grammar_focus: present simple, expressing preference (prefer, like better)

topics.title: A Typical School Day (Past or Present)
topics.description: Describe what school life is or was like for you.
topics.objective: Practise present or past simple depending on the learner's current situation.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Whether you're in school now or finished long ago, tell me — what was (or is) a typical school day like?
topics.instructions: Adapt tense based on whether the learner is currently studying. Ask about subjects, teachers, and memorable moments. Encourage full descriptive sentences.
topics.grammar_focus: past simple or present simple depending on context

topics.title: A Challenge You Overcame
topics.description: Talk about a difficult situation you faced and how you dealt with it.
topics.objective: Practise past simple and past continuous for describing a challenging experience.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Life often throws challenges at us — can you tell me about a difficult situation you managed to overcome?
topics.instructions: Encourage a clear narrative structure: situation, action, result. Mix past simple and past continuous naturally. Show empathy and ask follow-up questions about feelings.
follow_up_directions: a similar challenge for someone else
topics.grammar_focus: past simple and past continuous

topics.title: Plans for the Future
topics.description: Discuss your goals and plans for the next few years.
topics.objective: Practise future forms (going to, will, present continuous) for plans.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Let's look ahead a little — what are some things you're hoping to do in the next few years?
topics.instructions: Encourage a mix of future forms depending on certainty. Ask about career, personal, or travel goals. Push for specific details, not just vague answers.
topics.grammar_focus: future forms: going to, will, present continuous

topics.title: Being Environmentally Friendly
topics.description: Talk about how you try to help the environment.
topics.objective: Practise discussing habits and opinions related to sustainability.
topics.opening_message: Hi there! Environmental issues are on a lot of people's minds — what do you do to try to live more sustainably?
topics.instructions: Ask about recycling, transportation choices, and consumption habits. Encourage opinion language and modal verbs (should, could). Avoid being preachy; keep it conversational.
topics.grammar_focus: modal verbs for suggestions (should, could)

topics.title: A Book or Film That Impacted You
topics.description: Talk about a book or movie that made a strong impression on you.
topics.objective: Practise summarizing a story and explaining personal impact.
topics.opening_message: Hey! I'd love to know — is there a book or movie that really stuck with you after you finished it?
topics.instructions: Ask for a brief summary and then focus on why it mattered personally. Encourage linking words (because, so, which). Keep the summary short so the conversation flows.
topics.grammar_focus: linking words for cause and effect

topics.title: Dealing with Stress
topics.description: Discuss what causes you stress and how you manage it.
topics.objective: Practise discussing causes and solutions using varied vocabulary.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Everyone deals with stress sometimes — what usually causes you stress, and how do you handle it?
topics.instructions: Ask about specific triggers and coping strategies. Encourage varied vocabulary beyond 'stressed' (overwhelmed, anxious, calm). Be supportive, not clinical.
topics.grammar_focus: gerunds after prepositions (good at, worried about)

topics.title: Volunteering and Giving Back
topics.description: Talk about volunteer work you've done or would like to do.
topics.objective: Practise discussing motivations and experiences related to community service.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Some people love giving back to their community — have you ever volunteered for something?
topics.instructions: If they haven't, ask what cause they'd support and why. Encourage reasons and motivations using 'because' and 'in order to'. Explore feelings about helping others.
topics.grammar_focus: infinitive of purpose (in order to, to)

topics.title: Changes in Your Hometown
topics.description: Describe how your hometown has changed over the years.
topics.objective: Practise present perfect for changes over time.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Places change a lot over time — how has your hometown changed since you were a kid?
topics.instructions: Encourage present perfect structures (has become, has grown). Ask for specific examples: buildings, population, atmosphere. Compare past and present clearly.
topics.grammar_focus: present perfect for change over time

topics.title: Work-Life Balance
topics.description: Discuss how you balance work or study with personal life.
topics.objective: Practise discussing routines, priorities, and opinions.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Balancing work and personal life isn't always easy — how do you manage that balance yourself?
topics.instructions: Ask about specific strategies and challenges. Encourage opinion phrases and hypothetical language (if I had more time). Keep the tone reflective.
topics.grammar_focus: conditional sentences (if I had, I would)

topics.title: A Skill You'd Like to Learn
topics.description: Talk about a new skill you want to develop.
topics.objective: Practise future intentions and reasons for wanting to learn something.
topics.opening_message: Hi there! If you could learn any new skill this year, what would it be?
topics.instructions: Ask why they chose that skill and what steps they'd take to learn it. Encourage 'would like to' and future intention structures. Explore obstacles too.
topics.grammar_focus: would like to, expressing future intention

topics.title: Online Shopping vs In-Store Shopping
topics.description: Compare the experience of shopping online versus in physical stores.
topics.objective: Practise comparing two options and giving balanced opinions.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Shopping has really changed with the internet — do you prefer shopping online or going to actual stores?
topics.instructions: Encourage balanced comparison with pros and cons for each. Ask for specific examples of recent purchases. Use comparative and contrasting language.
topics.grammar_focus: contrasting language (whereas, on the other hand)

topics.title: Cultural Differences You've Noticed
topics.description: Talk about cultural differences you've experienced or observed.
topics.objective: Practise describing comparisons and personal observations across cultures.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Have you ever noticed something surprisingly different when learning about another culture?
topics.instructions: Ask for specific examples: food, customs, communication styles. Encourage comparative language and open-mindedness. Avoid stereotyping; focus on personal experience.
topics.grammar_focus: comparative structures, expressing surprise

topics.title: A Memorable Celebration
topics.description: Describe a wedding, birthday, or festival you remember well.
topics.objective: Practise narrating a past event with descriptive detail.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Celebrations often create great memories — can you tell me about one celebration you'll never forget?
topics.instructions: Ask about the event's atmosphere, people, and highlights. Encourage descriptive past tense narration. Help sequence the story logically.
follow_up_directions: food and music at the event
topics.grammar_focus: past simple narrative with descriptive adjectives

topics.title: How Technology Has Changed Relationships
topics.description: Discuss how technology affects the way people connect with each other.
topics.objective: Practise discussing cause and effect with present perfect and present simple.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Technology has changed a lot about how we communicate — do you think it's changed relationships for better or worse?
topics.instructions: Ask for both positive and negative examples. Encourage present perfect for change and present simple for current habits. Push for a personal opinion with reasons.
topics.grammar_focus: present perfect for change, cause-and-effect language

topics.title: Public Speaking and Confidence
topics.description: Talk about experiences with public speaking or building confidence.
topics.objective: Practise discussing feelings and strategies for overcoming nervousness.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Public speaking makes a lot of people nervous — how do you feel about speaking in front of others?
topics.instructions: Ask about specific experiences, good or bad, and coping strategies. Encourage adjectives for feelings and modal verbs for advice. Be encouraging throughout.
topics.grammar_focus: modal verbs for advice (should, could, might)

topics.title: The Impact of Remote Work
topics.description: Discuss how working or studying remotely has changed people's lives.
topics.objective: Practise discussing advantages, disadvantages, and personal opinions with more complex structures.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Remote work and online study became a lot more common recently — what do you think are the biggest effects of that shift?
topics.instructions: Push for balanced arguments with both pros and cons. Encourage complex sentences with linking words (although, however). Ask for personal or observed examples.
topics.grammar_focus: complex sentences with contrast connectors (although, whereas)

topics.title: Social Media and Mental Health
topics.description: Discuss the effects of social media on people's wellbeing.
topics.objective: Practise expressing nuanced opinions with supporting reasons.
topics.opening_message: Hey! There's a lot of debate about social media and mental health — where do you stand on that issue?
topics.instructions: Encourage the learner to consider multiple perspectives before giving their own opinion. Push for specific examples or evidence. Use hedging language (it seems, arguably).
topics.grammar_focus: hedging language, expressing nuanced opinion

topics.title: Consumerism vs Minimalism
topics.description: Discuss attitudes toward buying things versus living with less.
topics.objective: Practise debating two lifestyle philosophies with supporting arguments.
topics.opening_message: Hi there! Some people love collecting things, others prefer a minimalist lifestyle — which philosophy makes more sense to you?
topics.instructions: Ask the learner to justify their view with examples from their own life. Encourage counter-arguments to challenge their thinking. Use advanced vocabulary around consumption.
topics.grammar_focus: expressing and defending an argument

topics.title: The Role of AI in Daily Life
topics.description: Discuss how artificial intelligence is changing everyday life.
topics.objective: Practise discussing technology's societal impact with speculative language.
topics.opening_message: Hi! AI seems to be everywhere now, from phones to cars — how do you feel about its growing role in daily life?
topics.instructions: Ask about specific examples of AI they've encountered. Encourage speculative language about the future (might, could, is likely to). Explore both excitement and concerns.
topics.vocabulary_focus: artificial intelligence, automation, privacy, efficient, algorithm
topics.grammar_focus: speculative language (might, could, is likely to)

topics.title: Urbanization and City Life
topics.description: Discuss the growth of cities and its effects on society.
topics.objective: Practise discussing societal trends with cause-and-effect reasoning.
topics.opening_message: Hello! More and more people are moving to big cities around the world — why do you think that trend continues, and is it a good thing?
topics.instructions: Push the learner to identify causes and consequences. Encourage passive voice for describing trends (cities are being built). Ask for opinions on solutions to urban problems.
topics.grammar_focus: passive voice for describing trends

topics.title: The Value of Travelling
topics.description: Discuss what people gain from travelling to new places.
topics.objective: Practise articulating abstract benefits with supporting examples.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Some people say travel changes you as a person — do you agree, and why or why not?
topics.instructions: Push beyond surface-level answers ('it's fun') toward deeper reflection on personal growth. Encourage abstract nouns (perspective, growth, empathy) and examples. Challenge with a counterpoint if needed.
topics.vocabulary_focus: perspective, broaden, immerse, culture shock, appreciation
topics.grammar_focus: abstract nouns, supporting an argument with examples

topics.title: Balancing Tradition and Modern Life
topics.description: Discuss how people balance traditional values with modern lifestyles.
topics.objective: Practise discussing tension between two ideas with nuanced language.
topics.opening_message: Hey! A lot of people try to balance old traditions with a modern lifestyle — how do you see that balance playing out in your own life or culture?
topics.instructions: Ask for concrete examples of tradition versus modern pressures. Encourage nuanced connectors (while, despite, even though). Explore generational differences if relevant.
topics.grammar_focus: concessive clauses (while, even though, despite)

topics.title: Is Social Media Good for Society?
topics.description: Debate the overall impact of social media on society.
topics.objective: Practise constructing and defending a structured argument on a controversial topic.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Let's dig into a debate — overall, do you think social media has done more good than harm for society?
topics.instructions: Push for a clear thesis supported by multiple points. Challenge the learner with counter-arguments to strengthen critical thinking. Encourage sophisticated discourse markers (nevertheless, on balance).
topics.grammar_focus: discourse markers for argumentation (nevertheless, on balance, that said)

topics.title: Should Higher Education Be Free?
topics.description: Debate whether university education should be free for everyone.
topics.objective: Practise presenting and evaluating arguments on a policy question.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Here's a debate for you — should university education be free, or is that unrealistic? What's your take?
topics.instructions: Encourage the learner to weigh economic and social arguments on both sides. Ask about funding models and outcomes. Push for precise, academic-style vocabulary.
topics.grammar_focus: hypothetical and conditional structures for policy debate

topics.title: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
topics.description: Discuss ethical questions raised by advancing AI technology.
topics.objective: Practise reasoning through ethical dilemmas with abstract vocabulary.
topics.opening_message: Hi! As AI gets more powerful, some serious ethical questions come up — what worries or excites you most about that?
topics.instructions: Push the learner to consider multiple stakeholders (companies, workers, governments). Encourage abstract and academic vocabulary. Explore hypothetical scenarios to deepen the debate.
follow_up_directions: who is responsible when AI fails
topics.grammar_focus: hypothetical conditionals for ethical scenarios

topics.title: Individualism vs Collectivism
topics.description: Discuss the tension between individual freedom and collective responsibility.
topics.objective: Practise comparing philosophical viewpoints with sophisticated argumentation.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Different cultures value individual freedom versus the good of the group differently — where do you think the right balance lies?
topics.instructions: Encourage the learner to draw on cultural or historical examples. Push for nuanced positions rather than black-and-white answers. Model advanced connective phrases.
follow_up_directions: personal freedom vs public health rules
topics.grammar_focus: advanced connectives for nuanced argument (albeit, insofar as)

topics.title: The Future of Work
topics.description: Discuss how automation and changing economies might reshape careers.
topics.objective: Practise speculating about long-term societal change with sophisticated future forms.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Careers seem to be changing fast because of automation and shifting economies — what do you imagine work will look like in twenty years?
topics.instructions: Push for speculative, well-reasoned predictions rather than vague guesses. Encourage future perfect and modal speculation (will have changed, may well). Ask about implications for education and policy.
topics.vocabulary_focus: automation, reskilling, gig economy, obsolete, adaptability
topics.grammar_focus: future perfect and modal speculation (may well, is bound to)

topics.title: Is Happiness a Choice?
topics.description: Debate whether happiness is mostly a personal choice or shaped by circumstances.
topics.objective: Practise philosophical argumentation with abstract reasoning and examples.
topics.opening_message: Hello! Here's a thought-provoking one — do you think happiness is mostly something we choose, or is it shaped by our circumstances?
topics.instructions: Push the learner to support claims with reasoning, not just assertions. Encourage abstract vocabulary (fulfillment, contentment, resilience). Introduce a counterpoint to sharpen the argument.
topics.grammar_focus: abstract argumentation, concession and rebuttal

topics.title: Globalization: Benefits and Drawbacks
topics.description: Debate the overall effects of globalization on economies and cultures.
topics.objective: Practise weighing complex global issues with academic vocabulary.
topics.opening_message: Hi! Globalization connects economies and cultures more than ever — on the whole, do you see it as a positive force or a negative one?
topics.instructions: Push for a structured argument that acknowledges complexity and trade-offs. Encourage academic register and precise vocabulary. Ask for real-world examples to support claims.
topics.grammar_focus: academic register, hedging and qualifying claims

topics.title: Does Technology Make Us More Isolated?
topics.description: Debate whether modern technology brings people closer or drives them apart.
topics.objective: Practise constructing a balanced, evidence-based argument on a nuanced topic.
topics.opening_message: Hey! Some say technology connects us more than ever, others say it isolates us — after everything we've discussed today, what's your final take on that?
topics.instructions: Encourage the learner to synthesize ideas from earlier topics if relevant. Push for a clear concluding argument with supporting evidence. Model sophisticated summary language (in conclusion, taking everything into account).
topics.grammar_focus: summarizing and concluding an argument
